nodes.text:
Your immune system has nothing to do with it.

H5N1 isn’t common in humans because of its genetics.

It typically binds to the a2,3 linkages in birds respiratory tracts. That’s less prominent in humans and primarily in our digestive tract so to infect us a virus would need to pass the high acidity of the stomach.

Instead when the virus mutates to link with a2,6 which is found in the human respiratory tract, that’s when it can leap to humans.

High-viral loads, one of mutations, or weakened gut health, allow *one-off* cases to transfer from bird-to-human, whereas human-to-human transmission means a mutation in binder-preference from a2,3 to a2,6.

Because A/H5N1 is not antigenically similar to other flu strains your immune system will not recognize it. You will not have any memory B or T cells specific to the H5 subtype. And because the virus uses NS1 protein to block interferon signalling.

Therefore the body has no innate immune response to it.

It can only have a primary adaptive immune response which takes about 7-14 days to produce antibodies.

This is why, if human-to-human mutation is prominent the only thing that really matters is:

A) Viral load

&

B) Did it reach your lower respiratory tract where the a2,6 binding would be most likely & abundant.

Your immune system health does next to nothing here, and primarily determines how well you’ll handle the virus over all.

Whereas, washing your hands a bit more, or wearing a mask if you’re in a room full of sick people, lowers the viral load exposure, meaning a lower chance of infection.

If you are exposed to a direct high viral load, then no matter how healthy and strong your immune system is, you *will* get sick.

So you’ll be unwell for at least 5-7 days depending on when your immune system first detects it and you will feel like shit.

All of which can be avoided, by washing your hands a bit more frequently and taking precautions around sick people - not that fucking hard.

Lastly, if you already had A/H5N1 from the current strain, your bodies neutralizing anti-bodies only last about 6-12 months and assume no mutations.

Memory B cells and T cells last longer, 5-10 years for B cells, but those are disrupted by even small mutations.

T cells are 20 years but nullified by mutations. They also don’t prevent you getting sick, but instead fight off the virus and can take 7-14 days to generate.

So no, your immune system will not prevent you from getting sick.

And a “strong” immune system doesn’t matter if the body doesn’t recognize the disease, it will still take time to generate a response.

And the reason that novel illness like covid19 and non-human evolving influenza strains are problematic is specifically because your immune system can do absolutely nothing about it.

So please learn some science before trying to refute people on the internet, and stop spewing influencer pseudo-science bs.
